value: Like a hotel that accepts the passport your government issued, instead of issuing and checking an identity card of its own.
reason: A hotel checking you "with its own identity card" reads twice; the rewrite keeps the point that the relying party does not verify the credential itself.

value: It works as proof of identity for whoever presents it: validation is the only check, so the attacker can use it as their own.
reason: The old back restated the definition without saying what the attacker gains. SP 800-63C-4 p. 56: "can be presented on its own as proof of the identity of the party presenting it. No other proof beyond validation of the assertion is required."

value: No proof beyond validating a bearer assertion is required, which is why the guideline also restricts assertions to a single audience, to limit where replay can succeed.
reason: The old explanation repeated the back; single-audience restriction to limit replay is on the same page (SP 800-63C-4 3.13.4, p. 56).

value: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, SC-28(3) Protection of Information at Rest | Cryptographic Keys, PDF p. 344
reason: The evidence is control enhancement SC-28(3); the old label named SC-12(3) and a vague "SC-28 family discussion".

value: To control more precisely how guest systems are connected to each other; some hypervisors use VLAN standards for this.
reason: The front asks what a VLAN is used for, but the old back led with which hypervisors use it and buried the purpose. SP 800-125 p. 13: "use virtual LAN (VLAN) standards to allow better control of how the guest systems are connected."
Duplicates ccsp.operational-controls.capacity-planning-why (same CP-2(2) passage, same question); its concept moves to the card kept.

value: ccsp.availability-capacity-mgmt
ccsp.capacity-monitoring
reason: Takes over the concept of the deleted duplicate ccsp.cloud-infrastructure.capacity-planning.

value: The guide calls monitoring particularly important for traffic between two guests on one host, or between a guest and the host, because network sensors never see it.
reason: "Matters most" overstates the source: SP 800-125 p. 19 says "particularly important".

value: The focal point for an organisation's security operations and network defence: it monitors systems and detects, analyses and responds to incidents.
reason: SP 800-61r3 p. 15 only mentions outsourcing a SOC; it does not define one. The definition is in SP 800-53r5 IR-4(14), PDF p. 182.

value: Its purpose is to defend and monitor the organisation's systems and networks on an ongoing basis, so that incidents are handled in a timely manner.
reason: Re-cited to SP 800-53r5 IR-4(14) discussion, which states the SOC's purpose.

value: A security operations center (SOC) is the focal point for security operations and computer network defense for an organization. The purpose of the SOC is to defend and monitor an organization’s systems and networks (i.e., cyber infrastructure) on an ongoing basis. The SOC is also responsible for detecting, analyzing, and responding to cybersecurity incidents in a timely manner.
reason: Evidence for the new definition, verbatim from SP 800-53r5 IR-4(14).

value: NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5, Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations, IR-4(14) Security Operations Center, Discussion, PDF p. 182
reason: Re-cited to the passage that defines a SOC.

value: https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-53r5.pdf#page=182
reason: Re-cited to the passage that defines a SOC.

value: ITU-T Y.3500 (08/2014), Cloud computing: Overview and vocabulary, Annex A, Table A.2 Emerging cloud service categories, Management as a Service, PDF p. 15
reason: Management as a Service is not in clause 7.4; Y.3500 lists it in Annex A, Table A.2, as an emerging category (PDF p. 15).

value: Y.3500 lists Management as a Service among emerging cloud service categories, grouping service-level management with asset, change, capacity and problem management and the service catalogue.
reason: Says where the category sits (Annex A, emerging categories), as checked against Y.3500 PDF p. 15; facts only, in our own words.

value: It actually or imminently jeopardises, without lawful authority, the confidentiality, integrity or availability of information or a system, or violates law or security policies.
reason: The back dropped "without lawful authority", so lawful access would wrongly count. SP 800-61r3 p. 10: "actually or imminently jeopardizes, without lawful authority, the integrity, confidentiality, or availability".

value: Testers need expertise in network, operating system or application security, because the test shows how far adversaries could get within set limits of time, resources and skills.
reason: The constraints of time, resources and skills apply to the adversaries being modelled, not to the testers. SP 800-53r5 CA-8 p. 120: "penetration resistance of systems to adversaries within specified constraints. Such constraints include time, resources, and skills."

value: The control lists unscheduled and unauthorised changes alongside planned upgrades and modifications, so a change that skips the normal process is still covered.
reason: "Every kind of change" overstates; CM-3 lists specific kinds, including "unscheduled or unauthorized changes" (SP 800-53r5 p. 126).

value: Under the information sharing control, what can automated mechanisms help users check about personal data?
reason: "Besides law, what kind of access restriction…" reads twice and "besides law" is not in the source; the passage is under User-Based Collaboration and Information Sharing (AC-21), SP 800-122 p. 30.

value: Whether access authorisations match the access restrictions on the data, such as restrictions based on contracts.
reason: Matches the reworded front. SP 800-122 p. 30: "determining whether access authorizations match access restrictions, such as contractually-based restrictions, for PII."

value: Personal data can carry restrictions, such as contract terms, on who may access it; automated checks help users see whether an authorisation fits them before sharing.
reason: The old explanation repeated the back; this says why the check helps.
